paragraphs: An embodied agent moving through several rooms needs to connect what it sees now with observations and interactions from earlier. This paper proposes that inadequate spatial and temporal memory partly explains why language models struggle with such environments. It introduces both a benchmark for testing this ability and a model designed to improve it.

The benchmark, 3DMem-Bench, contains more than 26,000 trajectories and 2,892 embodied tasks, alongside question answering and captioning. The proposed model, 3DLLM-Mem, distinguishes current observations from stored experience. Tokens representing working memory query episodic memory, selectively retrieving and combining useful information about locations and events. This makes relevance to the current situation central to memory use.

The approach aims to preserve memory efficiency while supporting tasks that unfold over long periods. Experiments report state-of-the-art performance across various tasks, including a 16.5% success-rate improvement over the strongest baselines on the benchmark’s hardest in-the-wild embodied tasks. These results support selective memory fusion as a useful component of spatial and temporal reasoning.
neurips-2025-3dllm-mem-long-term-spatial.tldr: 3DLLM-Mem selectively combines current observations with stored experiences to improve reasoning and action in complex 3D environments.

paragraphs: Estimating gaze from a face image requires separating useful visual cues from facial details that do not indicate where someone is looking. Those extra details can encourage a model to overfit its training data, weakening performance in new settings. 3DPE-Gaze addresses this problem by explicitly separating gaze information using facial geometry and semantic concepts.

Its geometric module uses the FLAME face model to parameterize facial structure and appearance unrelated to gaze while extracting gaze features. A second module uses CLIP-guided contrastive learning to distinguish concepts relevant to gaze from irrelevant ones. The framework also incorporates three-dimensional facial landmarks as prior information, giving the estimator an explicit geometric reference.

The authors report that 3DPE-Gaze outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods on four cross-domain tasks. They highlight performance under lighting changes, extreme head orientations, and occlusion from glasses. These findings suggest that organizing face information around geometry and relevance can improve transfer across conditions, addressing the risk that a model learns incidental appearance patterns instead of useful gaze cues.
neurips-2025-3dpe-gaze-unlocking-the-pot.tldr: 3DPE-Gaze separates gaze-relevant information from distracting facial appearance using 3D geometry and semantic alignment.

paragraphs: Molecular property prediction often has too few labeled examples for effective learning. Auxiliary tasks can supply additional training signals, but choosing them requires expertise, and an extra task may fail to help the property prediction that actually matters. This paper introduces AutAuT to automate both task selection and the strength of each task’s contribution.

AutAuT uses large language models to retrieve auxiliary tasks, then integrates them through adaptive weighting based on gradient alignment. The central idea is to emphasize auxiliary tasks whose training directions agree with the primary objective. This connects the influence of an auxiliary task to its relationship with the main learning problem, reducing harmful contributions from irrelevant tasks.

The reported evaluations show improved predictive accuracy and performance exceeding 10 auxiliary-task approaches and 18 advanced molecular property prediction models. The contribution therefore combines automation with control over how additional supervision affects training. Its findings support selecting and weighting auxiliary tasks together, rather than assuming that adding more supervisory objectives will automatically improve molecular predictions.
neurips-2025-automatic-auxiliary-task-se.tldr: AutAuT automatically retrieves auxiliary learning tasks and weights them by alignment with the molecular property prediction objective.

paragraphs: Low-Rank Adaptation makes language-model fine-tuning economical, but predictions can become overconfident when training examples are scarce. Existing uncertainty-aware adaptations can overlook how uncertainty varies with the characteristics of an individual input. C-LoRA addresses this by making lightweight adaptation modules responsive to each sample’s context.

The method incorporates data-derived context into parameter posteriors, allowing uncertainty estimates to change with the input. This gives the model a mechanism for representing sample-specific uncertainty while retaining parameter-efficient fine-tuning. The authors report that this contextual treatment reduces overfitting, improves uncertainty calibration, and supports more robust predictions in few-shot settings.

Experiments with LLaMA2-7B show consistent improvements over state-of-the-art uncertainty-aware LoRA methods in uncertainty quantification and generalization. Ablation studies also support the importance of the contextual modules. The empirical scope is explicitly limited to 7B models: although the method is architecture-agnostic and could in principle apply at larger scales, its behavior there remains an open research question. The evidence therefore establishes benefits at the tested scale.
neurips-2025-c-lora-contextual-low-rank-.tldr: C-LoRA makes parameter-efficient fine-tuning sensitive to individual inputs, improving uncertainty estimates and generalization in experiments with 7B models.

paragraphs: Representing single-cell measurements through language creates a possible route for applying language models to cell biology. CellVerse asks how well those models actually perform on the resulting analysis tasks. It provides a unified question-answering benchmark combining four kinds of single-cell multi-omics data and three levels of biological analysis.

The tasks cover identifying cell types, predicting drug responses, and analyzing gene perturbations. The study evaluates 14 open- and closed-source models spanning 160 million to 671 billion parameters. This broad comparison examines whether the language-based approach supports useful decisions across distinct biological questions, rather than treating success on one task as evidence for all of them.

The results reveal substantial weaknesses. The evaluated specialist models, C2S-Pythia, fail to make reasonable decisions across the subtasks, while several generalist model families show preliminary understanding. Yet none of the tested models significantly improves on random guessing for drug response prediction. CellVerse therefore supplies evidence of specific capability gaps and a shared framework for measuring future progress.
neurips-2025-cellverse-do-large-language.tldr: CellVerse benchmarks language-based single-cell analysis and finds major gaps, including no significant advantage over random guessing in drug response prediction.

paragraphs: A reasoning benchmark can mislead when its questions or expected answers are unreliable. This paper examines that problem in knowledge-graph question answering, where systems must often connect several facts. A manual audit of 16 popular datasets finds an average factual correctness rate of only 57%, raising concerns about the evidence these benchmarks provide.

The identified issues include incorrect or incomplete answer annotations, ambiguous or unanswerable questions, trivial questions, and inconsistent or outdated knowledge. To address them, the authors introduce KGQAGen. It combines grounding in structured knowledge, language-model-guided question generation, and symbolic verification to produce examples intended to be both challenging and checkable.

The resulting KGQAGen-10k benchmark contains approximately 10,000 examples grounded in Wikidata. Evaluations show that even state-of-the-art knowledge-graph retrieval-augmented systems struggle on it. Together, the audit and new benchmark argue for treating data quality as part of reasoning evaluation itself: a difficult score is more informative when the questions and their supporting answers have been systematically constructed and verified.
neurips-2025-diagnosing-and-addressing-p.tldr: An audit exposes widespread knowledge-graph benchmark errors, and KGQAGen combines grounded generation with symbolic verification to build a more reliable benchmark.

paragraphs: Tiny objects in large, cluttered images pose a problem for multimodal language models whose input resolution limits visible detail. FineRS addresses this through a two-stage process that first identifies a promising region and then examines it more precisely. The aim is to connect instruction-based reasoning with accurate localization and segmentation.

Global Semantic Exploration produces a textual response and a coarse target region from the instruction and scene. Localized Perceptual Refinement then produces a more accurate bounding box and pixel-level mask. A retrospective reinforcement-learning reward couples the stages: the refined localization results help train the earlier exploration stage to choose better regions.

The paper also introduces FineRS-4k, a dataset targeting attribute-level reasoning and segmentation of subtle, small objects in complex high-resolution scenes. Evaluations on this dataset and public datasets report consistent improvements over state-of-the-art multimodal language-model approaches for reasoning and instruction-guided segmentation. The key contribution is making detailed localization feed back into the process that decides where to look.
neurips-2025-finers-fine-grained-reasoni.tldr: FineRS uses coarse-to-fine localization and a retrospective reinforcement-learning reward to reason about and segment extremely small objects.

paragraphs: Textual reasoning can compress away spatial relationships and fine visual details that matter for driving. FSDrive instead uses a predicted future image as an intermediate reasoning representation. Its visual chain of thought combines a future scene with coarse lane dividers and three-dimensional boxes, carrying information about both spatial structure and temporal change.

The same vision-language-action model first predicts that unified frame and then uses it with current observations to plan a trajectory. Training adds visual tokens and jointly teaches visual question answering and future-frame prediction. An easy-to-hard sequence begins with lane and box priors that impose physical constraints before moving to detailed future images.

On nuScenes and NAVSIM, the authors report more accurate trajectories and fewer collisions under ST-P3 and UniAD metrics. They also report competitive future-image generation quality and improved DriveLM scene understanding. These findings support visual intermediate reasoning as a way to narrow the gap between perception and planning and improve anticipatory behavior in the evaluated driving settings.
neurips-2025-futuresightdrive-thinking-v.tldr: FSDrive plans driving trajectories through predicted future images that combine scene detail with explicit spatial priors.

paragraphs: An image prompt can specify objects and relationships without explicitly resolving their placement or the steps needed to edit them. Generation Chain-of-Thought, or GoT, introduces a structured natural-language planning stage before synthesis. This stage describes semantic relationships, object attributes, and precise spatial coordinates that directly guide image generation or editing.

The authors construct datasets containing more than nine million examples with detailed semantic and spatial reasoning chains. Their implementation pairs Qwen2.5-VL, which produces the chains, with a diffusion model. A Semantic-Spatial Guidance Module connects the intermediate reasoning to visual synthesis, giving the image-producing system an explicit description of the intended composition.

Experiments report significant improvements over baselines on both generation and editing tasks. The intermediate representation also supports interaction: users can change reasoning steps to request precise image adjustments. The contribution is therefore both a generation method and a controllable interface, where composition decisions are expressed in language before they influence the final visual output.
neurips-2025-got-unleashing-reasoning-ca.tldr: GoT guides image generation and editing with explicit language-based plans describing object relationships, attributes, and spatial coordinates.

paragraphs: Dataset distillation creates a small synthetic training set intended to preserve the usefulness of a much larger dataset. Distribution-matching methods make this process efficient by aligning original and synthetic data without nested optimization. This paper argues that matching in ordinary Euclidean space overlooks hierarchical and geometric relationships within the data.

Hyperbolic Dataset Distillation embeds features from a shallow network into Lorentz hyperbolic space, whose geometry naturally accommodates tree-like structure. It then minimizes the geodesic distance between the centroids of original and synthetic features. This makes hierarchy part of the matching objective and guides synthetic examples toward root-centered regions while preserving underlying geometric characteristics.

Experiments on multiple datasets support the method’s effectiveness, and the authors report compatibility with most existing distribution-matching methods. They also find that pruning in hyperbolic space can retain model performance using only 20% of the distilled core set while improving training stability. This is an empirical result of their study, supporting geometry-aware compression rather than establishing a universal retention ratio.
neurips-2025-hyperbolic-dataset-distilla.tldr: HDD distills datasets by matching feature distributions in hyperbolic space to incorporate hierarchical structure.

paragraphs: Membership inference asks whether an attacker can identify examples that were used to train a model. This paper studies that privacy vulnerability in fine-tuned neural networks, focusing on how it changes with the number of training examples per class. It combines empirical analysis with theoretical analysis based on a simplified model of fine-tuning.

For models trained without differential privacy, the authors find that vulnerability decreases according to a simple power law as examples per class increase. Vulnerability is measured as attacker advantage at a fixed false-positive rate. Keeping that error rate fixed makes the reported relationship specifically about attack effectiveness under a consistent constraint on false accusations of membership.

A similar power-law relationship applies to the most vulnerable examples, but protecting those examples adequately requires a very large dataset. Thus, the relationship between dataset size and privacy does not imply that modest data growth protects everyone well. The study positions practical attack measurements as complementary to formal differential-privacy guarantees, while revealing how class-level data availability shapes exposure.
neurips-2025-impact-of-dataset-propertie.tldr: Membership-inference vulnerability falls with examples per class according to a power law, but the most exposed examples require very large datasets for adequate protection.

paragraphs: Generating long text from sensitive reference material raises the problem of incorporating useful information while providing formal privacy protection. InvisibleInk addresses this with a differential-private generation framework whose guarantees concern the sensitive reference texts. It interprets next-token sampling through the exponential mechanism, connecting language-model generation to a privacy mechanism.

The method reduces privacy cost by isolating the sensitive contribution to token scores relative to scores based on public information, then clipping only that contribution. It also improves generation quality by sampling from a small superset of the highest-ranked private tokens without additional privacy cost. These changes target both the information that must be protected and the token choices available during generation.

Empirical comparisons report at least an eightfold reduction in computation relative to state-of-the-art baselines at matched text utility across privacy levels. The authors also report high-quality private long-form generation at less than four-to-eight times the computation of non-private generation. The stated gains make privacy-preserving generation more computationally practical while retaining rigorous reference-text privacy guarantees.
neurips-2025-invisibleink-high-utility-a.tldr: InvisibleInk reduces the computational cost of differentially private long-form generation by isolating sensitive token-score contributions and improving private token sampling.

paragraphs: Predictions can help an online bidding algorithm make decisions, but relying on them creates a tradeoff between doing well when advice is useful and remaining reliable when it is poor. This paper studies that tradeoff when uncertainty appears in the prediction oracle or randomness appears in the algorithm itself.

The first part considers distributional predictions, which provide stochastic information rather than a single deterministic prediction. The authors derive Pareto-optimal algorithms for consistency and robustness. Here, optimality concerns the balance between the two goals: the algorithms achieve the best possible tradeoffs, rather than simply maximizing performance under favorable predictions without accounting for unfavorable ones.

The second part investigates randomized bidding algorithms and establishes upper and lower bounds on their consistency–robustness tradeoffs. These results describe both achievable performance and limits on what randomness can provide. Together, the two analyses extend prior work centered mainly on deterministic algorithms and prediction oracles without stochastic quality information, giving a theoretical account of how uncertainty changes useful algorithm design.
neurips-2025-learning-augmented-online-b.tldr: This paper characterizes optimal and bounded tradeoffs between prediction-based performance and robustness for stochastic online bidding.

paragraphs: Fine-tuning changes a language model’s internal representations, but understanding what those changes mean often requires extensive evaluation. This paper studies the geometry of contextual embeddings as another source of evidence. It measures local intrinsic dimensions, describing the dimensional structure around portions of the latent space, and tracks how those measurements change during training.

The authors find that mean local dimension provides information about several distinct training behaviors. Their examples connect it to exhausted training capability in dialogue state tracking, overfitting in emotion recognition, and grokking in an arithmetic task. These findings link an internal geometric measurement to changes in learning and generalization across the studied applications.

The experiments also suggest a practical heuristic: decreases in mean local dimension tend to accompany and anticipate later performance improvements. The wording matters because this is an observed tendency, not a universal rule that lower dimension guarantees a better model. The contribution offers practitioners an additional interpretive signal for understanding fine-tuning and configuring models for particular tasks.
neurips-2025-less-is-more-local-intrinsi.tldr: Changes in local embedding dimension provide empirical signals of training behavior, with decreases tending to precede performance gains.

paragraphs: Object-centric learning aims to represent a scene as distinct objects. Slot Attention does this through a set of feature vectors called slots, but a fixed slot count can split one object into multiple representations when scene object counts vary. MetaSlot introduces an adaptable alternative that can be integrated into existing object-centric architectures.

The method maintains a codebook of object prototypes learned by vector-quantizing slot representations. It uses this codebook to identify and remove duplicate slots from the aggregated representations. It also injects noise into the attention iterations, progressively reducing its strength to accelerate and stabilize aggregation. These components address both redundant object representations and the process that forms them.

Across multiple public datasets, models equipped with MetaSlot show significant gains on tasks including object discovery and recognition. The authors also report more interpretable slot representations than existing Slot Attention variants. The findings support adapting the representation to variable object counts, with the codebook providing a shared reference for consolidating redundant slots.
neurips-2025-metaslot-break-through-the-.tldr: MetaSlot uses learned object prototypes to remove duplicate slots and adapt object-centric representations to varying object counts.

paragraphs: Model editing seeks to correct a pretrained model efficiently without retraining it extensively. For vision transformers, existing approaches often borrow language-model editing techniques that modify multilayer perceptrons. This paper reports that vision-transformer predictions are more strongly influenced by multi-head self-attention modules, motivating a different location for targeted corrections.

The proposed framework first identifies the attention heads most responsible for an incorrect prediction. It then selectively removes the associated features to change that prediction. A learned projection matrix further refines image representations, helping balance the desired correction against stable predictions on unrelated data. The procedure therefore treats identifying the source of an error and limiting collateral changes as connected objectives.

Experiments across real-world datasets and model-editing benchmarks show consistent improvements over existing vision-transformer editing methods. The reported gains include generalization and locality: edits transfer better while preserving behavior outside the intended correction. The contribution highlights the value of designing editing methods around the architectural components that most influence the model being edited.
neurips-2025-model-editing-for-vision-tr.tldr: This vision-transformer editing method targets error-associated attention features while learning a projection to preserve unrelated predictions.

paragraphs: Graph convolutional networks can lose useful distinctions as information spreads through a graph, a problem known as over-smoothing. Much work addresses its effect on individual node predictions. This paper examines how it also weakens representations used to classify entire graphs and proposes MultiNet to preserve more discriminative information at that level.

MultiNet adaptively divides each graph into several subgraph views and applies view-specific convolution operations within them. Restricting information propagation through these local views mitigates over-smoothing and helps retain differences among node representations. The method then uses an alignment-based readout that establishes correspondences between nodes across different graphs when constructing graph-level representations.

The two components address complementary stages: local convolution controls how features become mixed, while aligned readout preserves local structural information when forming a whole-graph summary. Theoretical analysis and empirical studies support reduced graph-level over-smoothing and strong classification performance. The paper’s central message is that preserving local distinctions must extend through the final aggregation step used for graph classification.
neurips-2025-multinet-adaptive-multi-vie.tldr: MultiNet reduces graph-level over-smoothing through adaptive subgraph convolutions and a readout that preserves local structural distinctions.

paragraphs: Bilevel reinforcement learning nests one learning problem inside another, making its data requirements harder to analyze than those of a standard Markov decision process. The difficulty is compounded when the inner problem is non-convex. This paper establishes a sample-complexity bound of O(ε⁻³) for bilevel reinforcement learning in continuous state and action spaces.

The analysis uses the Polyak–Łojasiewicz condition together with the structure of the Markov decision process to obtain closed-form gradients. That condition is a substantive part of the theoretical setup, so the result should be understood within the analyzed setting. The authors also extend their approach to general bilevel optimization with non-convex inner problems, improving existing O(ε⁻⁶) bounds to O(ε⁻³).

A separate algorithmic contribution addresses the cost of estimating hypergradients, which express how outer objectives depend on inner optimization. The proposed method uses only first-order information and avoids Hessian computations. Together, the results strengthen theoretical understanding of sampling requirements and provide a computational approach intended to accommodate large-scale bilevel problems.
neurips-2025-on-the-sample-complexity-bo.tldr: Using the Polyak–Łojasiewicz condition, this work establishes O(ε⁻³) sample-complexity bounds and a Hessian-free algorithm for bilevel learning.

paragraphs: Estimating an object’s three-dimensional position and orientation can admit several plausible answers, especially when symmetry makes different poses difficult to distinguish. RFMPose treats category-level pose estimation as a generative problem. It learns deterministic pose trajectories through Riemannian Flow Matching, bringing the geometry of the pose space directly into the modeling process.

Geodesic interpolation and bi-invariant metric constraints maintain geometric consistency. Riemannian Optimal Transport redistributes probability mass to reduce symmetry-related ambiguity without ad-hoc design. The framework also estimates likelihoods end to end using Hutchinson trace approximation, avoiding dependence on auxiliary models. These components combine geometric trajectory construction, ambiguity handling, and likelihood estimation within one approach.

On Omni6DPose, the authors report state-of-the-art performance, including gains of 4.1 on IoU25 and 2.4 on the 5°2cm metric over prior generative methods. They also report robust simulation-to-real transfer and extensions to pose tracking with minimal architectural changes. The results support geometry-aware generative modeling as a useful approach to pose estimation with multiple plausible hypotheses.
neurips-2025-rfmpose-generative-category.tldr: RFMPose uses Riemannian Flow Matching to estimate object poses while respecting geometry and addressing symmetry-induced ambiguity.

paragraphs: Improving language-model reasoning commonly requires labeled reasoning traces, verified answers, or pretrained reward models. Entropy Minimized Policy Optimization, or EMPO, explores whether unlabeled questions alone can provide a useful training signal. The paper presents it as an early attempt at fully unsupervised reasoning incentivization, without those external sources of supervision.

EMPO minimizes semantic entropy on the model’s answers to unlabeled questions. This directs optimization toward reduced uncertainty at the level of answer meaning. The training objective therefore comes from the model’s responses rather than a supplied correct answer or externally trained evaluator. The paper also provides preliminary analysis intended to explain why this objective can help.

Reported accuracy rises from 33.7% to 51.6% for Qwen2.5-Math-7B Base on math benchmarks and from 32.1% to 50.1% for Qwen2.5-7B Base on MMLU-Pro. The authors describe the resulting performance as competitive with supervised counterparts. These experiments show that the proposed unsupervised objective can produce substantial reasoning gains in the tested settings.
neurips-2025-right-question-is-already-h.tldr: EMPO improves reasoning on tested benchmarks by minimizing semantic entropy on unlabeled questions without external supervisory signals.

paragraphs: This paper studies learning single-index models with squared error when labels may contain adversarial noise. The input distribution is assumed to be Gaussian. Its main result is a computationally efficient algorithm achieving a constant-factor approximation across all monotone activation functions satisfying a bounded-moment condition of order 2 + ζ, where ζ is positive.

That function class includes monotone Lipschitz activations as well as discontinuous functions such as possibly biased halfspaces. The breadth matters because earlier results for unknown activations either lacked constant-factor approximation or covered substantially smaller families. The result therefore expands the activation types supported by an efficient robust-learning guarantee under the stated distributional and moment assumptions.

The algorithm’s conceptual contribution is an optimization framework guided by a useful vector field rather than ordinary gradient methods. Its update directions exploit the learning problem’s structure, properties of Gaussian spaces, and regularity associated with monotonicity. This shows how problem-specific update rules can establish guarantees for a broader function class, including cases with discontinuities and corrupted labels.
neurips-2025-robustly-learning-monotone-.tldr: A vector-field-guided algorithm efficiently learns broad classes of monotone single-index models under Gaussian inputs and adversarial label noise.

paragraphs: Occupancy prediction estimates which parts of three-dimensional space are occupied and assigns semantic labels to them. Nighttime images complicate this task because different regions can be too dark or excessively bright. LIAR addresses these uneven conditions by using illumination information throughout image enhancement and the construction of spatial representations.

Its selective enhancement stage uses daytime illumination priors to decide whether a nighttime image actually needs global brightening. The resulting illumination maps then guide two further components. Two-dimensional sampling uses larger position offsets in darker regions and smaller offsets in brighter ones to reduce underexposure-related feature degradation. Three-dimensional projection constructs illumination intensity fields and supplies refined residual queries to improve semantic understanding in overexposed regions.

This design treats darkness and excessive brightness as distinct problems requiring different interventions. Experiments on real and synthetic datasets report superior performance in challenging nighttime conditions. The findings support using illumination as an explicit guide for feature sampling and spatial refinement, extending the role of lighting information beyond initial image enhancement.
neurips-2025-see-through-the-dark-learni.tldr: LIAR improves nighttime 3D occupancy prediction by using illumination maps to guide selective enhancement, feature sampling, and spatial refinement.

paragraphs: SpecMAS converts a natural-language operating procedure into an executable formal system model and checks whether that model satisfies specified properties. It identifies operational modes, variables, and transitions, then generates code in NuSMV syntax. The goal is to connect informal descriptions with a verification process that produces explicit, checkable results.

A dedicated reasoning agent extracts both stated and implicit properties from the procedure. Temporal-logic model checking evaluates these properties against the generated model. When verification fails, a debugging agent analyzes the counterexample and revises the model. This correction loop continues until the properties are satisfied, making verification an active part of model construction.

The paper describes this loop as providing provable correctness by construction for the generated model against the extracted properties. Representative case studies demonstrate generality, correctness, and practical feasibility, and the authors propose a benchmark for comparing model-checking performance. The contribution brings generation, property extraction, formal checking, and counterexample-based repair into one autonomous workflow with an interpretable basis for its verification results.
neurips-2025-specmas-a-multi-agent-syste.tldr: SpecMAS generates formal models from operating procedures and iteratively repairs them using model-checking counterexamples until extracted properties are satisfied.

paragraphs: Text2MBL translates descriptions of modular building layouts into executable Building Information Modeling code. Its output is a parametric layout with semantic information, generated through code instantiation. This connects a high-level design request to a structured building representation that can participate in automated workflows, extending beyond a two-dimensional layout.

The framework addresses three organizational levels: physical modules, self-contained dwelling units, and functional rooms. An object-oriented code architecture represents this hierarchy, while fine-tuned language models generate structured sequences of actions in code. The hierarchy is central because the output must capture how these different building elements relate within a modular housing design.

The authors curate paired textual descriptions and reference layouts from real modular housing projects for training and evaluation. Assessment covers whether the code executes, whether its meaning matches the description, and whether the geometry is consistent. The contribution is a unified pipeline linking language understanding to executable BIM generation, with evaluation focused on the distinct requirements of usable structured layouts.
neurips-2025-text-to-code-generation-for.tldr: Text2MBL turns modular housing descriptions into executable BIM code organized around modules, dwelling units, and rooms.

paragraphs: Pretrained diffusion models can generate trajectories guided by a task’s rewards, but standard gradient guidance becomes less effective with non-convex objectives, non-differentiable constraints, or multiple rewards. Tree-guided Diffusion Planner addresses these settings through structured search at test time. It uses pretrained models and test-time reward signals without task-specific training.

The planner organizes trajectory generation as a tree search with two sampling levels. Training-free particle guidance first produces diverse parent trajectories for broad exploration. Fast conditional denoising then refines sub-trajectories according to task objectives. This combines exploration across different candidate regions with more focused improvement within them, allowing gradient information to operate over a wider solution space.

Evaluations cover maze gold-picking, robot-arm block manipulation, and multi-goal AntMaze exploration. The authors report that TDP consistently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches on all three tasks. These findings support tree-structured exploration and refinement as a way to improve test-time planning flexibility, especially where local gradient guidance alone struggles with the structure of the objective.
neurips-2025-tree-guided-diffusion-plann.tldr: TDP combines diverse trajectory exploration with targeted denoising in a tree search to improve planning using pretrained diffusion models.
